raw_response:
I've been farming this same land for 30 years. My father farmed it before me. I know this soil — it's loam, holds water reasonably well, but if I don't irrigate the wheat during jointing it will suffer. I don't need to think hard about what to do this year. I'll do what I've been doing, with small adjustments from what worked last year and what the neighbors are doing.

**My thinking:**

My 10 mu is all in the same fields — wheat goes in after October, maize goes in after June wheat harvest. Same land, two crops. I leave a little as paths and edges, so I plant about 10 mu of each.

For **wheat**, I'll buy the Jimai variety from the supply co-op in town. Everybody here uses it. It's resistant to rust and yields well. I apply base fertilizer before sowing — compound fertilizer plus some urea. Then I top-dress nitrogen at jointing. I'll irrigate three times: once before winter freeze-up, once at jointing, once at heading. Four would be better but the pump costs money and my son isn't always home to help. I spray herbicide early and watch for aphids and powdery mildew in spring — two spray rounds usually handles it.

For **maize**, I'll use Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed — same as last year, gave me over 550 jin per mu. Maize goes in right after wheat harvest, I direct seed it, no tilling — saves time and the ground is already loose enough. Summer rains help but I'll irrigate once at tasseling if it's dry, maybe twice. I apply urea in splits — some at planting, rest at V6. One herbicide pass early, maybe one more for corn borer if I see damage.

I don't do potassium much — my soil tests from the village extension a few years back said it's not deficient. I'll add a little phosphorus in the base compound fertilizer.

We have 8 people at home but four of them work in town or in the factory. Farming is mainly me and my wife, sometimes my older son on weekends. So I keep things manageable.
